newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines C Bank sees inflation lower than 6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippines C Bank sees inflation lower than 6 pct.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank said on Thursday inflation in the coming months is expected to be lower than 6.0 percent after inflation fell to a 10-year low in May.
"We are more confident that the inflation rate for the ensuing months will be lower than 6.0 percent, the lower end of the original inflation target," the Central Bank said in a statement.
Analysts expect inflation in the second half to be higher than in the first half of the year because it would be computed from a lower base in the comparable period last year.
Earlier, the National Statistics Office said inflation declined to a ten-year low of 4.2 percent in May compared with 4.6 in April.
"At only 4.2 percent, inflation for May was 2.1 percentage points lower than the programme of 6.3 percent," Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson said.
"It is indeed welcome news that the average inflation for the first five months of 1997 was further brought down to 4.6 percent," he added.
Last week, the government said it was revising downwards its inflation target for 1997 to between 5.2 to 5.7 percent compared with an earlier forecast of 6.0 to 6.5 percent.
"For the Central Bank, we will sustain prudence in monetary growth, stability in interest rates, and continued market orientation of the exchange rate," Singson said.
